newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia corn prices down on import arrivals.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia corn prices down on import arrivals.

text.p: Indonesian corn prices were easier on Tuesday on the back of ample stocks and arrivals of imports from China and as the country's general election campaign kept the market lethargic, traders said.

Corn was quoted at 385-395 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, compared with 400 rupiah a week ago, as 50,000 tonnes of Chinese corn arrived. Feedmills were expected to take delivery of another 50,000 tonnes during the month.

"The market has ground to a halt because of the election," one trader said. "There is very little consumer demand, while imports will cost a bit more because of the rupiah's weakness against the U.S. dollar.
"Although the rupiah has strengthened a little after it fell against the dollar just before the start of the campaign, it remains weak."

Indonesians vote in national polls on May 29, with the ruling Golkar party certain to win in the face of a split in the opposition Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) and the limited appeal of the Moslem-oriented United Democratic Party (PPP).
The traders said Chinese corn was being offered at $150 a tonne C&F, while U.S. shipments were quoted at $157-$160.
"Chinese corn remains more attractive than U.S. corn because of the price and shorter sailing time," one trader said. "We can also buy Chinese corn in small quantities.

"The Chinese corn that has arrived and is expected to arrive through the month was ordered about two months ago," he said. "The market is now very quiet because feedmills have ample stocks or are waiting for their imports to arrive."
The traders expressed surprise at the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) leaving ending soybean stocks unchanged at 125 million bushels.
"I am very surprised," one trader said. "It is much more than I had expected. It looks like the offtakes have not been as much as expected."
The CBOT July soybean contract fell 20-1/2 U.S. cents to close at $8.68-1/2 a bushel on Monday after USDA said 1996/97 soybean ending stocks were unchanged at 125 million bushels.
The news disappointed the market, which had anticipated a cut of five million to 10 million bushels.
The trader said local buyers were expected to stay out of the market waiting for soymeal prices to fall further before taking positions. "I see them sitting it out for a while."
Local soymeal prices were quoted steady at 870-880 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, against 870 rupiah last week.
